title: EvidenceEntropy: Information-Theoretic Quantification of Trust-Significance Dependence in Cochrane Meta-Analyses
body: How much information does knowing a meta-analysis trust grade provide about whether its finding is statistically significant? We computed Shannon entropy, mutual information, and Kullback-Leibler divergence for 6,229 Cochrane meta-analyses across 14 clinical domains, treating trust grade as a six-level categorical variable and significance as binary. Information measures were derived from empirical contingency tables with normalized mutual information providing a scale-free comparison metric. Overall mutual information was 0.037 bits with normalized mutual information of 0.033, indicating that trust grades carry modest but non-zero predictive information about significance status. Neurological meta-analyses showed the highest normalized mutual information at 0.312 while renal showed near-zero values, and the Kullback-Leibler divergence between trust-weighted and naive significance distributions was 0.611 bits overall. Trust grade provides limited but detectable information gain over naive significance assessment, with marked variation across clinical specialties. These measures assume discrete grade categories and may underestimate dependence present in the continuous trust score.
